description: Labelled ground-truth corpus for the perimeter-access-audit skill. Each case names the exact findings the audit must emit and, by omission, every finding it must not. Clean cases carry an empty expectation on purpose: they are the false-positive control, and a detector without one has no measured precision.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Ordinary permissive robots.txt and a conforming llms.txt.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Scoped disallows plus Crawl-delay. A path rule is not a root block.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: BOM, CRLF, lowercase directives, odd spacing, and a comment naming GPTBot. Parsing must be structural, not substring matching.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: SEO crawlers blocked at the root; no AI agent affected.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: A misconfigured host serving an HTML 404 body at /robots.txt with status 200.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: No robots.txt. Under the exclusion protocol absence permits everything, so it is neither a finding nor an unknown.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Groups named Fetch, Claude and Search disallow the root. Under substring group matching these capture Meta-ExternalFetcher, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot and OAI-SearchBot. Under RFC 9309 exact-token matching they capture nothing. Minimised from a real site that triggered exactly this.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: A conforming llms.txt using `*` list markers. Markdown treats `-`, `*` and `+` identically; accepting only one reported a correct real-world file as malformed.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: The host answers /llms.txt with its own HTML page. No file is published, so this is an absence, not a malformed file.

cases.label: defect

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Every AI agent disallowed while conventional crawlers stay allowed. One finding, not three.

cases.label: defect

cases.label: defect

cases.label: defect
